items.stem: Which statement about a bacterial cell is correct?

options.text: Its genetic material is held inside a nucleus.
Its cell wall is made from cellulose fibres.
Its width is close to that of a cheek cell.
Its genetic material is a single DNA loop.

items.why: The genetic material of a bacterial cell is not enclosed in a nucleus: it is a single DNA loop, and there may also be one or more small rings of DNA called plasmids.

items.stem: Which parts are found in most animal cells?

options.text: Cytoplasm, ribosomes and a cellulose wall
Cytoplasm, mitochondria and cell sap
Cytoplasm, ribosomes and mitochondria
Cytoplasm, ribosomes and a large vacuole

items.why: Most animal cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm, a cell membrane, mitochondria and ribosomes, so all three parts listed here are present.

items.stem: Which statement about plant cells is correct?

options.text: Their cell walls are found in animals too.
Their cell walls are made of cellulose.
Their chloroplasts are in every plant cell.
Their vacuoles are found in animals too.

items.why: Plant and algal cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, which strengthens the cell.

items.stem: Which statement about cell differentiation is correct?

options.text: Most animal cells differentiate at an early stage.
Most plant cells differentiate at an early stage.
Most cells differentiate by growing to a bigger size.
Most animal cells differentiate to repair damage.

items.why: As an organism develops, cells differentiate to form different types of cell, and most types of animal cell differentiate at an early stage.

items.stem: In a mature animal, what is cell division mainly used for?

options.text: Cell division has stopped in mature animals.
Cell division makes the cells grow larger.
Cell division repairs and replaces cells.
Cell division continues as the animal grows.

items.why: In mature animals, cell division is mainly restricted to repair and replacement.

items.stem: Why can an electron microscope be used to study cells in much finer detail than a light microscope?

options.text: It magnifies the image very many more times.
It has higher magnification and resolution.
It finds the real size from the image size.
It uses a much stronger lens to enlarge cells.

items.why: An electron microscope has much higher magnification and resolving power than a light microscope, so it can be used to study cells in much finer detail.

items.stem: Why should cultures be incubated at a maximum temperature of 25°C in a school laboratory?

options.text: It reduces the growth of harmful pathogens.
It is the temperature for fastest growth.
It stops condensation forming on the lid.
It matches the body temperature of humans.

items.why: In school and college laboratories cultures are incubated at a maximum of 25°C, because this reduces the likelihood of growing pathogens that could harm people.

items.stem: Why is a Petri dish stored upside down after the agar gel has been inoculated?

options.text: To stop the agar falling out of the dish.
To stop condensation dripping onto the agar.
To keep the culture warm enough to grow.
To hold the lid firmly against the agar.

items.why: With the dish upside down, condensation collects on the lid below the agar gel and cannot drip onto its surface, so the culture stays uncontaminated.

items.stem: A cheek cell is 6 × 10⁻⁵ m wide and a bacterial cell is 2 × 10⁻⁶ m wide. About how many times wider is the cheek cell?

options.text: About 3 times wider
About 300 times wider
About 30 times wider
About 0.03 times wider

items.why: 6 × 10⁻⁵ divided by 2 × 10⁻⁶ is 3 × 10¹, so the cheek cell is about 30 times wider. This is the order of magnitude difference between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.

items.stem: A muscle cell contains large numbers of mitochondria. What is the function of these mitochondria?

options.text: To transfer energy by aerobic respiration
To make energy needed for contraction
To join amino acids into new proteins
To store the glucose used in exercise

items.why: Mitochondria are where aerobic respiration takes place, transferring the energy the cell needs. A muscle cell needs a great deal of energy, so its structure includes many mitochondria.

items.stem: A plant cell is 0.06 mm long. On a drawing of the cell, the nucleus is about one tenth of the length of the cell. What is the best estimate of the real diameter of the nucleus?

options.text: 0.6 mm

items.why: The estimate from the drawing is that the nucleus is one tenth of the cell length, so its real diameter is 0.06 mm / 10 = 0.006 mm. This judges the relative size of a sub-cellular structure.

items.stem: Root hair cells have a long, thin extension that reaches out into the soil. How does this help the cell to carry out its function?

options.text: It makes the cell larger so it can work faster.
It exposes the chloroplasts to more sunlight.
It allows a thicker cellulose wall to form.
It increases the surface area for absorption.

items.why: The structure of the root hair cell relates to its function in the plant: the extension gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions from the soil.

items.stem: The image of a cell is 10 mm wide. The real cell is 0.05 mm wide. What is the magnification?
items.why: magnification = size of image / size of real object = 10 mm / 0.05 mm = 200. Both measurements are in the same units, so the magnification has no units.

items.stem: One bacterium divides once every 20 minutes. How many bacteria will there be after 2 hours?

options.text: 12 bacteria
64 bacteria
7 bacteria
120 bacteria

items.why: There are 6 divisions in 2 hours at one division every 20 minutes, and the population doubles each time, so the number is 1 × 2⁶ = 64.

items.stem: One bacterium divides once every 20 minutes. What is the number of bacteria after 5 hours, expressed in standard form?
items.why: 5 hours gives 15 divisions, so the number is 2¹⁵ = 32 768, which is 3.3 × 10⁴ to two significant figures in standard form.

items.stem: A clear area around a colony on an agar plate is 20 mm across. What is its cross-sectional area?

options.text: 314 mm²
1257 mm²
63 mm²
31.4 mm²

items.why: The radius is half of 20 mm, so r = 10 mm and the cross-sectional area is πr² = π × 10² = 314 mm².

items.stem: Which statement about chromosomes and genes in a body cell is correct?

options.text: A gene is made of a large number of chromosomes.
Each chromosome carries one gene made of DNA.
Each chromosome in the nucleus is found singly.
Each chromosome carries a large number of genes.

items.why: The nucleus of a cell contains chromosomes made of DNA molecules, and each chromosome carries a large number of genes.

items.stem: How are the chromosomes normally arranged in a body cell?

options.text: Singly, inside the nucleus of the cell.
In pairs, inside the nucleus of the cell.
In pairs, inside a large gene in the cell.
In pairs, carrying a single gene per pair.

items.why: In body cells the chromosomes are normally found in pairs, and the chromosomes are contained in the nucleus of the cell.

items.stem: Before a cell divides it grows and increases its number of ribosomes and mitochondria. What happens to the DNA at this stage?

options.text: The DNA is halved to leave one copy of each chromosome.
The DNA replicates after the nucleus has divided in two.
The DNA is altered so the two new cells are different.
The DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome.

items.why: Before a cell can divide the DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome, which is how the genetic material is doubled.

items.stem: What happens during mitosis and the stage that follows it?

options.text: One set of chromosomes goes to each end, then the cytoplasm divides.
One set of chromosomes goes to each end, and the cell remains whole.
Half of each chromosome goes to each end, then the cytoplasm divides.
The chromosomes are shared unevenly, then the cytoplasm divides.

items.why: In mitosis one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell and the nucleus divides; finally the cytoplasm and cell membranes divide to form two identical cells.

items.stem: Which statement describes a stem cell?

options.text: A specialised cell that carries out one particular function.
A bone marrow cell that forms most cell types in the body.
An undifferentiated cell that can give rise to other cells.
A plant cell taken from the meristem tissue of a plant.

items.why: A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell of an organism which is capable of giving rise to many more cells of the same type, and from which certain other cells can arise from differentiation.

items.stem: Which statement about therapeutic cloning is correct?

options.text: The stem cells produced are rejected by the patient's body.
The stem cells are taken from the patient's bone marrow.
An embryo with the same genes as the patient is produced.
The cells produced are specialised for one particular job.

items.why: In therapeutic cloning an embryo is produced with the same genes as the patient, and stem cells from the embryo are not rejected by the patient's body so they may be used for medical treatment.

items.stem: Which statement about treatment with stem cells is correct?

options.text: It is a guaranteed cure for conditions such as paralysis.
It uses bone marrow stem cells to replace nerve cells.
It fails because the patient's body rejects the cells.
It may be able to help conditions such as paralysis.

items.why: Treatment with stem cells may be able to help conditions such as diabetes and paralysis.

items.stem: Which statement about the risks of using stem cells is correct?

options.text: Viral infection could be transferred to the patient.
The concerns are ethical rather than medical ones.
Cells from a cloned embryo are rejected by the body.
The cells cannot give rise to more cells of one type.

items.why: The use of stem cells has potential risks such as transfer of viral infection, and some people have ethical or religious objections.

items.stem: Which description gives the three overall stages of the cell cycle in the correct order?

options.text: The cell grows and copies its DNA, then the nucleus divides, then the cytoplasm divides.
The nucleus divides first, then the cell grows and copies its DNA, then the cytoplasm divides.
The cell grows and halves its DNA, then the nucleus divides, then the cytoplasm divides.
The cell grows and copies its DNA, then the nucleus divides, and division is complete.

items.why: Before a cell can divide it grows and the DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome; in mitosis one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell and the nucleus divides; finally the cytoplasm and cell membranes divide to form two identical cells.

items.stem: A human body cell containing 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. What does each new cell contain?

options.text: 23 chromosomes, identical to the parent cell
46 chromosomes, different from the parent cell
46 chromosomes, identical to the parent cell
23 chromosomes, different from the parent cell

items.why: During the cell cycle the genetic material is doubled and then divided into two identical cells, so each new cell has the parent cell's 46 chromosomes.

items.stem: A cut on the arm of a fully grown adult heals as new skin cells are produced. Which statement about the new cells is correct?

options.text: New cells with half the chromosomes are made.
New identical cells are produced by mitosis.
New genetically different cells are produced.
Mitosis has stopped because the adult is grown.

items.why: Cell division by mitosis produces two identical cells and is important in the growth and development of multicellular organisms, which includes producing new skin cells in this context.

items.stem: Which statement about the function of stem cells is correct?

options.text: Meristem tissue can differentiate into any type of plant cell.
Bone marrow stem cells can differentiate into any type of cell.
Embryonic stem cells are specialised for one particular job.
Meristem tissue stops making new cells as the plant matures.

items.why: Meristem tissue in plants can differentiate into any type of plant cell, throughout the life of the plant.

items.stem: Why are stem cells from meristems used to clone rare plant species?

options.text: Different plants are produced quickly and economically.
Identical plants are produced quickly and economically.
Identical plants are produced slowly and at a high cost.
Identical plants are produced while the parent is young.

items.why: Stem cells from meristems in plants can be used to produce clones of plants quickly and economically, so rare species can be cloned to protect them from extinction.

items.stem: In diffusion, the particles of a substance in solution show a net movement:

options.text: from a lower to a higher concentration, requiring energy
from a lower to a higher concentration, using no energy
from a higher to a lower concentration, without energy
from a higher to a lower concentration, requiring energy

items.why: Diffusion is the spreading out of the particles of any substance in solution, or particles of a gas, resulting in a net movement from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration, and it does not require energy from respiration.

items.stem: Osmosis takes place through a partially permeable membrane. Which statement describes it correctly?

options.text: Water moves from a concentrated solution to a dilute one
Water moves from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one
Sugar moves from a dilute solution to a concentrated one
Solutes move from a concentrated solution to a dilute one

items.why: Osmosis is the diffusion of water from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane.

items.stem: The concentration of oxygen in the air inside the alveoli is raised. Everything else, including the temperature, stays the same. What happens to the rate of diffusion of oxygen into the blood?

options.text: It falls, as a steeper gradient crowds particles
It stays the same, as the temperature has not risen
It falls, as the particles collide with one another
It rises, as the concentration gradient is steeper

items.why: The difference in concentrations (concentration gradient) is a factor which affects the rate of diffusion, so raising the oxygen concentration in the alveoli increases the rate at which oxygen diffuses into the blood.

items.stem: Cube A has sides 1 mm long. Cube B has sides 2 mm long. Which statement about their surface area to volume ratios is correct?

options.text: Cube A has a ratio of 3:1; cube B has a ratio of 6:1
Cube A has a ratio of 6:1; cube B has a ratio of 3:1
Cube A has a ratio of 3:1; cube B has a ratio of 12:1
Cube A has a ratio of 6:1; cube B has a ratio of 12:1

items.why: Cube A: surface area 6 mm2, volume 1 mm3, ratio 6:1. Cube B: surface area 24 mm2, volume 8 mm3, ratio 3:1. The smaller cube has the relatively large surface area to volume ratio, as a single-celled organism does.

items.stem: Which feature of the alveoli in the lungs increases the effectiveness of gas exchange?

options.text: A thick wall holding the gases in for longer
A small surface area that packs the cells in
A thin wall giving a short diffusion path
A thick wall that slows the escape of gases

items.why: The effectiveness of an exchange surface is increased by a membrane that is thin, to provide a short diffusion path, so oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse quickly between the alveoli and the blood.

items.stem: A potato cylinder has a mass of 4.0 g at the start. After 30 minutes in a sugar solution its mass is 3.4 g. What is the percentage loss of mass, and how is it found?

options.text: 17.6%, dividing the change by the final mass
15.0%, dividing the change by the starting mass
85.0%, dividing the final mass by the start mass
117.6%, dividing start mass by the final mass

items.why: The change in mass is 4.0 g minus 3.4 g, which is 0.6 g. Percentage loss of mass = (0.6 divided by 4.0) multiplied by 100 = 15.0%, using the starting mass of the plant tissue.

items.stem: Root hair cells take up mineral ions from a very dilute solution in the soil. How are the mineral ions taken up?

options.text: By active transport, which uses energy from respiration
By diffusion, moving down the concentration gradient
By osmosis, across the partially permeable membrane
By diffusion, moving up the concentration gradient

items.why: Active transport moves substances from a more dilute solution to a more concentrated solution, against a concentration gradient, and requires energy from respiration. This allows mineral ions to be absorbed into plant root hairs from very dilute solutions in the soil.

items.stem: Why do large multicellular organisms need specialised exchange surfaces and a transport system?

options.text: Their surface area to volume ratio is too small for diffusion
Their surface area to volume ratio is too high for diffusion
Their surface area to volume ratio increases as they get bigger
Their surface area to volume ratio grows with their surface area

items.why: A single-celled organism has a relatively large surface area to volume ratio, which allows sufficient transport of molecules to meet its needs. In a large multicellular organism the ratio is too small for diffusion across the outer surface to supply enough molecules, so surfaces and organ systems are specialised for exchanging materials and a transport system carries them to the cells.

items.stem: A student plots percentage change in mass of potato cylinders on the y-axis against concentration of sugar solution on the x-axis. The line crosses the x-axis, at zero percentage change in mass, at 0.30 mol/dm3. What does this point show?

options.text: Water moved into the cells from the sugar solution
Water moved out of the cells into the sugar solution
The sugar moved from the solution into the cells
The cells and the solution had equal concentrations

items.why: At zero percentage change in mass there is no net movement of water by osmosis, so the cell contents and the external solution are at the same concentration, and 0.30 mol/dm3 is the concentration inside the potato cells.
